story.heading: The story of Parral in three scenes
story.intro: Three questions about Hidalgo del Parral. Each answer comes live from the data, with what is known and what is not.

storm.title: 1. The storm of 1 July 2026
storm.text: On 1 July 2026, a storm left streets under water in Parral and swept a vehicle along the Arroyo de las Quintas. Chihuahua Civil Protection recorded 22.8 mm of rain in one hour. Did the satellite pass while it lasted?
storm.source: Source: bulletin of the State Civil Protection Coordination, Government of Chihuahua (1 July 2026)

monsoon.title: 2. A date pair in the rainy season
monsoon.text: From 16 to 28 August 2026, in the middle of the summer rainy season. This is what the radar says about that date pair, and what it cannot prove.
monsoon.showOnMap: Show this pair on the map

mine.title: 3. A point next to the La Prieta Mine
mine.text: The La Prieta Mine is part of Parral's mining history. We took a point next to it, according to OpenStreetMap, and looked at what the radar detected in each date pair.
mine.count: {{same}} of {{total}} pairs with no detectable change at this point.
mine.note: Detecting no change is also information, but it does not prove that nothing changed: it says the radar saw no change larger than its threshold.

event.heading: Could the satellite see an event?
event.intro: Tell us when something happened (a storm, a river flood, a wildfire) and we will tell you whether NISAR passed over the area while it lasted. It does not say whether anything changed.
event.timeHelp: In Parral, UTC is local time plus 6 hours: 15:37 in Parral is 21:37 UTC.
event.error: The check could not be done. Review the date and try again.

state.observable: Observable: there was a pass while the event lasted

event.observableNote: This does not say that anything changed: for that, look at the verdict for the date pair that includes that pass.
